name: Chippewa River
gaugeName: CHIPPEWA RIVER AT CHIPPEWA FALLS, WI
blurb: Chippewa River paddles across Wisconsin, including short urban trips below Dells Dam in Eau Claire. Start at Forest Street or Phoenix Park and finish at Hobbs Landing, or explore other listed stretches. Several longer itineraries still have unresolved dam and portage questions.

timing.note: A reviewed speed/flow calibration has not been established. Access and guide information remain available.

notices.title: Cornell Dam portage required
notices.text: The Cornell city ramp is above the dam. Use the established canoe/kayak carry on the west side to reach the downstream put-in. FERC describes a roughly 1,000-foot portage; Xcel’s recreation map shows its location. Stay away from the dam and use the designated re-entry, not the informal fishing area immediately below it. Confirm current access and signs before launching.
notices.sourceName: Xcel Energy — Cornell recreation facilities map

sections.notes: This river-and-lake trip requires a land carry around Wissota Dam. The county-published Area 178 map identifies a canoe portage on the west side of Lake Wissota. Access markers show approximate facilities. The preliminary 11.1-mile river distance does not include walking or carry time; check wind and lake conditions as well as river flow.
sections.routeReview: The county plan’s Area 178 map labels the canoe portage around Wissota Dam. This access map does not draw its shoreline entrances or walking route, and no continuous dotted line crosses the dam. Inspect the current signed carry and downstream launch before committing to the trip.

notices.title: Wissota Dam: portage required
notices.text: Use the canoe portage shown on the west side in the county’s Area 178 map (appendix page 80). Check the signed exit, trail and downstream re-entry during your shuttle, including whether you can carry your boat. Stay away from the spillway and powerhouse; do not paddle through the dam.
notices.sourceName: Chippewa County — forest plan appendix, Area 178 map

notices.title: Dam releases can change conditions quickly
notices.text: Xcel warns of rapidly changing currents near its dams. Follow posted restrictions and warning signals, remain outside buoy lines, and keep clear of spillways and powerhouse outlets. A published carry map does not establish today’s water or trail conditions.

notices.title: Finish above Dells Dam
notices.text: Take out at Mount Simon Park. Dells Dam is farther downstream; this short pond trip does not include the dam or a portage. Identify the landing before launching and obey dam warnings and restricted areas.
notices.sourceName: Visit Eau Claire — Chippewa River Water Trail map

sections.notes: Mount Simon Park is above Dells Dam. Begin with the published land carry to the Forest Street Greenway / Eau Claire Maintenance carry-in below the dam, then paddle to Hobbs Landing. For a trip that starts below the dam, choose the separate Forest Street–Hobbs section. The preliminary 4.1-mile river distance does not include carry time.
sections.routeReview: The water-trail map shows a land portage from Mount Simon Park along the Addison Street, Sheridan Road and Forest Street corridor to the below-dam carry-in. The carry and exact shoreline connections are not drawn here. Do not float from Mount Simon through Dells Dam.

notices.title: Dells Dam: portage required
notices.text: Start with the land carry shown in the linked water-trail map, from Mount Simon Park to the Eau Claire Maintenance / Forest Street carry-in below Dells Dam. Inspect the public approach and current signs before bringing your boat. A vehicle shuttle to the below-dam launch is another option.
notices.sourceName: Visit Eau Claire — Chippewa River Water Trail map, 2016 edition

notices.title: Urban river hazards below the dam
notices.text: The guide identifies old log pilings, rapids near Lake Street Bridge and a rock ledge near Little Niagara Creek. Releases can change the current. Take out at Hobbs on river right, facing downstream; the guide warns of additional hazards beyond that landing.
notices.sourceName: Visit Eau Claire — Chippewa River Water Trail guide
